M. genitalium: persistent nongonococcal urethritis after doxycycline; separate NAAT
HSV: painful ulcers and external dysuria rather than isolated cervical discharge
Cystitis: suprapubic tenderness, bacteriuria; urethritis → **distal anterior vaginal wall tenderness**, sterile pyuria

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.name: Chromosomal and genetic disorders
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.scope: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Turner syndrome (45,X0), Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY), Fragile X syndrome (FMR1 trinucleotide repeat), Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes, DiGeorge syndrome (22q11 deletion)
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.core: Recognize syndromic combinations of growth, cognition, gonadal function, dysmorphism, and congenital malformations; confirm with the correct genetic test.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced maternal age: meiotic nondisjunction; balanced parental translocation: recurrent aneuploid pregnancy
Family expansion history: repeat disorders; microdeletions often de novo

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Down** (trisomy 21): hypotonia, upslanting fissures, epicanthal folds, macroglossia, single palmar crease, AV septal defect
DiGeorge: conotruncal defect, cleft palate, absent thymus, hypocalcemic tetany
Turner: newborn hand/foot lymphedema, redundant nuchal skin; later nevi
**Williams** (7q11.23 deletion): overfriendly, elfin facies, hyperacusis, intellectual disability, supravalvular stenosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **Genomic imprinting**: parent-specific expression; deletion or uniparental disomy can disrupt the active copy
22q11 deletion disrupts pharyngeal pouch development → T-cell deficiency and hypoparathyroidism

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected Down, Turner, Klinefelter → **karyotype**; prenatal screening alone never establishes diagnosis
Microarray: microdeletion; targeted repeat analysis: fragile X; methylation testing: imprinting disorders
Down: assess heart, hearing, vision, thyroid; DiGeorge: calcium and lymphocyte subsets

rows.label: Tx
items: Early developmental services, speech support; repair congenital defects
Turner: growth hormone then estrogen/progestin; Klinefelter: testosterone after endocrine assessment
Prader-Willi: supervised food access; Angelman: seizure management; DiGeorge: calcium and infection management

rows.label: Complications
items: Down: duodenal atresia (double bubble), leukemia, early Alzheimer disease, atlantoaxial instability
Turner: coarctation, bicuspid valve, aortic dissection; Klinefelter: infertility, breast cancer
Prader-Willi: severe obesity; DiGeorge: severe infections and later psychiatric disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Genetic counseling**: recurrence depends on nondisjunction, translocation, imprinting mechanism, or repeat expansion
Avoid live vaccines with severe T-cell deficiency; use irradiated blood for profound immunodeficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Noonan syndrome: Turner-like habitus, normal chromosomes; either sex, pulmonic stenosis
Congenital hypothyroidism: hypotonia and delayed development; abnormal newborn thyroid screen
Constitutional delay: delayed bone age; no edema or nevi
Rett: girls with regression; MECP2 variant

table.title: Distinctive genotype–phenotype pairs
rows: Short female, webbed neck, streak ovaries, primary amenorrhea
Tall male, small firm testes, gynecomastia, high FSH/LH
FMR1 CGG expansion at X fragile site; silencing
Long face, large ears, macroorchidism, autism-like behavior
IUGR, clenched overlapping fingers, prominent occiput, micrognathia, VSD

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established genetics teaching.

colorectal-cancer-screening.name: Colorectal cancer screening
colorectal-cancer-screening.scope: Average-risk screening age 45-75, colonoscopy, FIT, high-risk screening (family history, Lynch syndrome, IBD), post-polypectomy surveillance
colorectal-cancer-screening.core: Screen average-risk adults ages 45–75; every positive noncolonoscopy screening test requires diagnostic colonoscopy.

rows.label: Who
items: Average risk: no CRC/adenoma history, IBD or hereditary syndrome; FDR = first-degree relative
★ Symptoms or iron deficiency anemia → **diagnostic evaluation**, regardless of screening age
FDR CRC/advanced polyp <60 or ≥2 affected FDRs → high-risk family pathway

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Ages 76–85: individualize by health, preference and prior screening; stop after 85
★ High-risk family → start **40 or 10 years before youngest diagnosis**, whichever earlier
Family-risk colonoscopy every 5 years; one FDR ≥60 → start 40, routine intervals

rows.label: Test
items: ★ **Colonoscopy every 10 years** or **FIT annually** are common strategies
Stool DNA–FIT every 1–3 years; CT colonography every 5 years
Flexible sigmoidoscopy every 5 years, or every 10 years plus annual FIT

rows.label: IF positive
items: Positive FIT/stool DNA/CT study → colonoscopy; repeating stool test cannot clear the result
Post-polypectomy intervals assume complete removal, adequate preparation and high-quality examination

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Lynch: colonoscopy roughly age 20–25 every 1–2 years; gene/family history can modify
Colonic IBD: surveillance about 8 years after onset; PSC → begin at diagnosis
Routine stool testing between scheduled high-quality surveillance colonoscopies adds little benefit

congenital-infections.name: Congenital infections
congenital-infections.scope: Cytomegalovirus (sensorineural hearing loss, periventricular calcifications), Toxoplasmosis (chorioretinitis), Parvovirus B19 (hydrops), Rubella, Varicella, Zika, screening and diagnosis
congenital-infections.core: Congenital infection causes growth restriction, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, thrombocytopenia, or hydrops; organ-specific patterns identify the pathogen.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CMV: toddler saliva/urine; toxoplasma: undercooked meat, cat feces; B19: child with slapped-cheek rash
Absent rubella/varicella immunity; mosquito exposure or sexual transmission in Zika-risk areas

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae/blueberry-muffin lesions, abnormal fetal ultrasound; many infected newborns initially appear well
★ B19 hydrops: cardiomegaly, ascites, edema without red-cell alloantibodies
Maternal rash: B19 → slapped cheek, then reticular limb rash; rubella → descending rash, postauricular nodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transplacental infection disrupts organogenesis; later exposure may cause inflammation or marrow suppression
Toxoplasma transmission increases with gestational age; earlier infection causes more severe injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal exposure → pathogen-specific **IgG/IgM**, paired titers or avidity; isolated IgM needs confirmation
★ CMV newborn diagnosis: saliva PCR then confirm urine PCR **within 21 days**
Suspected fetal infection → targeted ultrasound, pathogen-specific amniotic-fluid PCR; B19 → serial MCA Doppler
Prenatal rubella IgG routinely; no universal US maternal CMV, toxoplasma, or B19 screening

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic congenital CMV → **valganciclovir**, monitor CBC and liver tests
Congenital toxoplasmosis → pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin; maternal regimen depends on fetal infection
B19 severe fetal anemia → intrauterine transfusion; rubella/Zika structural injury → supportive care
Maternal varicella exposure without immunity → varicella-zoster immune globulin; maternal pneumonia → IV acyclovir
Maternal varicella onset 5 days before to 2 days after delivery → **newborn VZIG**

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, neurodevelopmental disability; delayed/progressive hearing loss requires longitudinal audiology

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Rubella/varicella vaccination before pregnancy or postpartum; **live vaccines contraindicated during pregnancy**
Handwashing after diapers; cook meat, avoid litter handling; mosquito precautions and Zika exposure counseling
Term newborn of varicella-immune mother: transplacental IgG protects → no prophylaxis after exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aneuploidy: abnormal genetic testing rather than pathogen testing
Rh disease: positive maternal antibody screen with fetal anemia

table.title: Discriminating congenital patterns
rows: Periventricular calcifications, microcephaly, sensorineural hearing loss, chorioretinitis
Severe microcephaly, subcortical calcifications, ocular abnormalities

congenital-infections.evidence: CMV testing checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/cytomegalovirus/hcp/clinical-overview/index.html); remaining pathogen patterns established teaching.

contraception.name: Contraception
contraception.scope: Combined oral contraceptives, progestin-only pills, implant, intrauterine devices, tubal sterilization
contraception.core: Choose contraception through shared decisions about efficacy, bleeding, reversibility, adherence, and estrogen-related vascular risk.

rows.label: Who
items: Anyone seeking pregnancy prevention; adolescents and nulliparous patients can use IUDs or implants
Healthy patient: blood pressure suffices; **no pelvic exam** needed before oral contraceptives

rows.label: Schedule
items: Pills daily; depot medroxyprogesterone every 3 months; implants/IUDs last years (product-dependent)
★ Emergency contraception ≤**5 days**: copper IUD/ulipristal; levonorgestrel ≤72 h, no medical contraindications
Progestin-only pills: daily timing crucial; norethindrone less forgiving than drospirenone

rows.label: Special groups
items: Breastfeeding (estrogen lowers milk volume, protein) or estrogen contraindication → progestin-only or copper IUD
Current breast cancer → copper IUD; avoid hormonal methods
Prior VTE, poor adherence → **IUD/implant** (depot raises VTE risk); older exams: depot, avoid IUD after STI

rows.label: Choice
items: Combined pills: suppress ovulation, improve acne/cramps, reduce endometrial/ovarian cancer risk
★ **LARC** minimizes adherence failures; condoms add STI protection
Tubal sterilization: permanent; counsel regret, alternatives, surgical risk, ectopic risk after failure

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Estrogen: **migraine with aura, prior VTE/thrombophilia**, hypertension (stop pill), early postpartum
Smoking age ≥35: combined methods usually avoid; ≥15 cigarettes/day → absolute contraindication
IUD: pregnancy, cervicitis/PID, distorted cavity (non-distorting fibroid OK); copper: also Wilson disease

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Same-day STI screening need not delay insertion without cervicitis; prior PID alone permits IUD
Sterilization: voluntary informed consent; no required partner approval, parity, or marital status
After ulipristal, wait 5 days before progestin; backup contraception needed after hormonal restart

table.title: Long-acting choices
rows: Treats heavy menses; atrophy → expected benign amenorrhea

dysmenorrhea.name: Dysmenorrhea
dysmenorrhea.scope: Primary dysmenorrhea, secondary dysmenorrhea (endometriosis, adenomyosis, cervical stenosis), hematometra, NSAIDs, combined oral contraceptives
dysmenorrhea.core: Painful menstruation: primary disease begins after ovulatory cycles develop; later-onset, progressive, or refractory pain suggests pelvic pathology.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Early menarche, heavy/prolonged flow, family history, smoking
Prior cervical excision/ablation → stenosis; endometriosis and adenomyosis produce secondary symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Suprapubic cramping radiating to back/thighs, nausea, diarrhea, headache
★ **Dyspareunia, abnormal bleeding, infertility**, or pain outside menses → secondary cause
Amenorrhea or scant flow after cervical procedure with cyclic pain → retained menstrual blood

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Progesterone withdrawal → endometrial prostaglandins → uterine hypercontractility and ischemia
Outflow obstruction traps blood in uterine cavity → hematometra

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Classic adolescent presentation without red flags → **clinical diagnosis**, no initial imaging
Sexual activity → pregnancy test; infection risks → gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Secondary features → pelvic examination and **transvaginal ultrasound**; transabdominal imaging if needed
No improvement after 3–6 months despite adherence → investigate secondary disease, consider laparoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NSAIDs**, starting 1–2 days before expected bleeding through first 2–3 days
★ Inadequate response/contraception desired → **combined OCP** or progestin; continuous suppression may help
Heat, exercise; avoid NSAIDs with active ulcer disease or significant renal dysfunction
Treat underlying lesion; cervical stenosis with hematometra → cervical dilation/drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: School/work absence, sleep disturbance; untreated secondary disease may impair fertility
Analgesic adverse effects: GI bleeding, renal injury; estrogen-containing contraception → VTE risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Track cycles and preempt pain; ongoing menstrual suppression reduces recurrence when pregnancy not desired

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, nonmenstrual bleeding, possible instability
PID: fever, mucopurulent discharge, cervical motion tenderness

table.title: Secondary patterns
rows: Posterior nodularity; ultrasound may be normal
Heavy bleeding, boggy uniformly enlarged uterus

dysmenorrhea.evidence: Not checked online; established adolescent gynecology and pelvic-pain teaching.

early-pregnancy-loss.name: Early pregnancy loss
early-pregnancy-loss.scope: Threatened abortion, inevitable abortion, incomplete abortion, complete abortion, missed abortion, anembryonic pregnancy
early-pregnancy-loss.core: First-trimester bleeding requires pregnancy location and viability assessment before labeling miscarriage or choosing expectant, medical, or surgical management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Embryonic aneuploidy most common; maternal age, prior losses, uterine anomalies, antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Clues
items: Cramping, vaginal bleeding, passage of tissue; symptoms may be absent with retained nonviable pregnancy
★ Hypotension, syncope, peritoneal signs → **hemorrhage or ruptured ectopic**
Fever, uterine tenderness, foul discharge → septic abortion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryonic/fetal demise or failed embryonic development → decidual separation and variable cervical dilation
Corpus luteum progesterone sustains pregnancy until ~10 weeks; removal earlier → **progesterone supplementation**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transvaginal ultrasound** plus quantitative β-hCG; CBC, blood type, pelvic examination
Definitive nonviability: CRL ≥7 mm without heartbeat or mean sac diameter ≥25 mm without embryo
Absent embryo/heartbeat on repeat: ≥11 days after yolk sac, ≥14 days after sac-only → nonviable
No intrauterine pregnancy → serial hCG/ultrasound; tissue passage alone cannot exclude ectopic

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable, infected, or uncontrolled hemorrhage → **urgent uterine aspiration**; sepsis → IV broad-spectrum antibiotics
Confirmed stable loss → patient choice: observation, mifepristone followed by misoprostol, or aspiration
Threatened loss → expectant follow-up; bed rest does not prevent miscarriage
Stable, unlocated pregnancy, falling hCG → serial hCG until negative; no methotrexate
★ Rh-negative loss **≥12 weeks → RhIg**; ACOG omits routine testing earlier; older exam questions may expect Rh typing

rows.label: Complications
items: Retained products, infection, hemorrhage; intrauterine adhesions after instrumentation; grief/depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking/alcohol avoidance, optimize diabetes; most isolated chromosomal losses unpreventable
Recurrent clinical losses → assess uterine anatomy, antiphospholipid antibodies and selected genetic causes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine implantation, adnexal mass/free fluid
Gestational trophoblastic disease: very high hCG, abnormal cystic intrauterine tissue
Subchorionic hematoma: bleeding without cramping; viable intrauterine pregnancy, perichorionic collection
Normal early pregnancy: spotting, 5-week sac, hCG ~1,000, simple corpus luteum cyst; embryo not yet expected

endometrial-cancer.name: Endometrial cancer
endometrial-cancer.scope: Endometrial hyperplasia, endometrioid adenocarcinoma, uterine sarcoma (leiomyosarcoma, carcinosarcoma, radiation risk), unopposed estrogen, biopsy, staging
endometrial-cancer.core: Postmenopausal bleeding warrants endometrial evaluation; chronic unopposed estrogen drives hyperplasia and endometrioid carcinoma.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, chronic anovulation/PCOS, nulliparity, early menarche, late menopause, estrogen without progestin
Tamoxifen, Lynch syndrome; prior pelvic radiation increases uterine sarcoma risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Abnormal uterine bleeding, watery/bloody discharge; pelvic pain or enlarged uterus with advanced disease
Growing postmenopausal uterine mass → consider sarcoma; growth rate alone cannot establish malignancy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Postmenopausal adipose aromatase: **androstenedione → estrone**, unopposed estrogen
Atypical hyperplasia/endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia: premalignant lesion with frequent concurrent carcinoma
Serous/clear-cell cancers: aggressive, estrogen-independent; carcinosarcoma classified as high-grade carcinoma
Leiomyosarcoma: malignant myometrial smooth muscle, usually de novo rather than transformation of benign leiomyoma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AUB at **≥45 years**, or younger with persistent bleeding/estrogen risks → endometrial biopsy
★ ACOG 2026: most postmenopausal bleeding → **TVUS plus tissue sampling**
Classic ≤4 mm reassurance rule changed; persistent bleeding always requires histology, regardless of thickness
Insufficient/negative blind biopsy with continued symptoms → hysteroscopy-directed biopsy; Pap does not exclude disease
Surgical staging assesses myometrial/cervical invasion, nodes, extrauterine spread; sarcoma can escape endometrial sampling

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Operable carcinoma → **total hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy**, sentinel-node assessment
Advanced/high-risk disease → stage-directed radiation and systemic treatment; carboplatin/paclitaxel commonly used
Suspected sarcoma → intact uterine removal; avoid uncontained morcellation

rows.label: Complications
items: Anemia, metastasis, recurrence; lymph-node surgery → lymphedema

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Weight management; add **progestin to systemic estrogen** when uterus intact; evaluate Lynch families

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginal atrophy: thin friable mucosa; malignancy still needs exclusion
Leiomyoma: usually premenopausal, well-circumscribed smooth-muscle mass

table.title: Hyperplasia
rows: Progestin, often levonorgestrel IUD; repeat sampling
Hysterectomy; selected fertility preservation: progestin + serial biopsies

endometrial-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG bleeding update 2026](https://www.acog.org/news/news-releases/2026/04/acog-publishes-updated-guidance-evaluation-postmenopausal-bleeding), [EIN consensus](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/clinical-consensus/articles/2023/09/management-of-endometrial-intraepithelial-neoplasia-or-atypical-endometrial-hyperplasia); other content established teaching.

endometriosis.name: Endometriosis
endometriosis.scope: Pelvic endometriosis, deep infiltrating endometriosis, endometrioma (chocolate cyst), uterosacral nodularity, cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, laparoscopy, medical management
endometriosis.core: Reproductive-age patient with progressive cyclic pelvic pain, deep dyspareunia, and infertility from ectopic endometrial tissue.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Early menarche, short cycles, prolonged menstruation, family history; obstructed menstrual outflow

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Uterosacral nodularity**, fixed retroverted uterus, posterior cul-de-sac tenderness
Dyschezia or cyclic rectal bleeding → bowel involvement; urinary cyclic symptoms → bladder disease
Pain severity poorly correlates with lesion burden; examination may be normal

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Estrogen-responsive implants provoke inflammation, fibrosis, adhesions, and distortion of pelvic anatomy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical assessment + **transvaginal ultrasound** first; normal imaging cannot exclude superficial disease
MRI maps deep lesions or indeterminate adnexal masses; CA-125 not a diagnostic test
★ **Laparoscopy with biopsy**: definitive test; for uncertain diagnosis, refractory symptoms, or planned operative treatment
Current ACOG: presumptive clinical diagnosis, no surgery before empiric treatment; older exams may expect laparoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain, no immediate pregnancy goal → **NSAID + continuous combined OCP** or progestin
Persistent symptoms → GnRH agonist/antagonist with add-back hormones to limit hypoestrogenic adverse effects
Refractory disease or selected infertility → laparoscopic excision/ablation and adhesiolysis
Endometrioma surgery may reduce ovarian reserve; balance pain, suspicion, size, and fertility goals
Trying to conceive → fertility evaluation; hormonal suppression does not improve spontaneous conception

rows.label: Complications
items: Adhesive infertility, bowel/ureteral obstruction, chronic pain; small increase in clear-cell/endometrioid ovarian cancer
GnRH suppression → hot flashes, bone loss; disease may recur after conservative surgery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Postoperative hormonal suppression reduces pain recurrence when pregnancy not desired; no established primary prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Adenomyosis: diffusely enlarged, boggy uterus with heavy bleeding
PID: fever, discharge, cervical motion tenderness; pain less cyclic
Primary dysmenorrhea: normal examination, onset soon after menarche, no structural lesion

table.title: Anatomic forms
rows: Fibrotic nodules involving ligaments, bowel, bladder
Ovarian chocolate cyst; homogeneous ground-glass ultrasound echoes

epilepsy.name: Epilepsy
epilepsy.scope: Focal seizures, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, absence seizures, juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, EEG findings, antiepileptic therapy (valproate, levetiracetam, lamotrigine), lifestyle counseling
epilepsy.core: Recurrent unprovoked seizures reflect epilepsy; classify focal versus generalized onset before choosing a maintenance antiseizure drug.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior brain injury, stroke, CNS infection, developmental lesions, genetic predisposition
Sleep deprivation, alcohol withdrawal and missed drugs can precipitate seizures; provoked seizures alone ≠ epilepsy

rows.label: Clues
items: Focal onset: aura, unilateral motor activity, automatisms or impaired awareness; may evolve bilaterally
Generalized tonic-clonic: abrupt loss of consciousness, stiffening/jerking, postictal confusion, lateral tongue injury
Absence: staring, immediate recovery; JME: morning myoclonus ± generalized convulsions
Infantile spasms: flexion clusters, **hypsarrhythmia** on EEG; standard antiseizure drugs ineffective

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormally synchronized cortical neuronal discharges impair awareness, sensation or motor function
Excitatory/inhibitory imbalance may arise from structural lesions or inherited channel/network dysfunction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **EEG and epilepsy-protocol MRI** after unprovoked seizure; normal EEG does not exclude epilepsy
Epilepsy: ≥2 unprovoked seizures >24 hours apart, or one with high recurrence risk/defined syndrome
Check glucose/electrolytes and provoking causes; urgent CT for trauma, focal deficit or persistent altered consciousness
Absence: generalized **3-Hz spike-wave**, provoked by hyperventilation; JME: generalized polyspike-wave
Child, nocturnal facial twitching/drooling, speech arrest + **centrotemporal spikes** → benign rolandic epilepsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Convulsion **≥5 minutes** → airway/glucose, **lorazepam**, then IV levetiracetam/fosphenytoin/valproate
Focal epilepsy → lamotrigine or levetiracetam; generalized tonic-clonic/JME → broad-spectrum agent
★ Valproate effective for generalized syndromes; **avoid when pregnancy possible** if alternatives effective
Pure absence → ethosuximide; absence + tonic-clonic → broad-spectrum drug; infantile spasms → **ACTH or vigabatrin**
Avoid carbamazepine/phenytoin for absence/myoclonic syndromes; drug-resistant focal disease → surgical evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Status epilepticus, injury, aspiration, SUDEP; valproate → hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, teratogenicity
Lamotrigine → serious rash with rapid titration
Levetiracetam → irritability/mood symptoms; depression history + high recurrence risk → continue, monitor mood
Erythromycin (CYP3A4 inhibitor) ↑carbamazepine → ataxia, somnolence, diplopia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Adherence, regular sleep, avoid alcohol excess; no abrupt drug withdrawal
Driving restrictions follow local law; no unsupervised swimming/heights; preconception folate and drug review
Pregnancy lowers antiseizure levels; breakthrough seizures → **increase current drug dose**, avoid switching

rows.label: Mimics
items: Syncope: prodrome, rapid recovery; brief jerks possible
Psychogenic nonepileptic events: video-EEG confirms typical event without epileptic correlate

table.title: Focal seizure localization
rows: Epigastric/olfactory aura, lip-smacking automatisms; superior quadrantanopia

epilepsy.evidence: Pregnancy recommendations checked 2026-10-30: [AAN/AES/SMFM 2024](https://www.aan.com/PressRoom/Home/PressRelease/5170); classification established teaching.

fetal-growth-restriction.name: Fetal growth restriction
fetal-growth-restriction.scope: Symmetric vs asymmetric FGR, uteroplacental insufficiency, chromosomal anomalies, congenital infections, umbilical artery Doppler surveillance, oligohydramnios
fetal-growth-restriction.core: Estimated fetal weight or abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile requires evaluation for placental dysfunction and fetal disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal hypertension, preeclampsia, renal/vascular disease, smoking, cocaine, malnutrition, prior affected pregnancy
Aneuploidy, structural anomalies, CMV; multiple gestation

rows.label: Clues
items: Fundal height lag >3 cm, decreased movement, oligohydramnios; sometimes abnormal maternal placental disease markers
★ **EFW <3rd percentile** indicates severe disease; normal-size parents do not establish constitutional smallness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental resistance reduces oxygen/nutrients; redistribution preserves cerebral over abdominal growth
Low fetal renal perfusion reduces urine production and fluid volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Ultrasound biometry using reliable dating → detailed anatomy; serial growth generally every 3–4 weeks
★ **Umbilical artery Doppler every 1–2 weeks**; absent (AEDV)/reversed (REDV) diastolic velocity → intensified surveillance
Weekly NST after viability; increase frequency with Doppler deterioration or maternal comorbidity
Early <32 weeks, unexplained or anomalous → offer amniocentesis/microarray; CMV PCR if amniocentesis chosen
Do not order indiscriminate TORCH panels without exposure or suggestive findings

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Reversed flow → **hospitalization**, corticosteroids, frequent cardiotocography, delivery planning
Anticipated preterm birth → betamethasone; magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection before 32 weeks
Nonreassuring testing/maternal deterioration → earlier delivery; absent/reversed flow may favor cesarean
Bed rest, sildenafil, and LMWH solely to treat/prevent FGR provide no established benefit

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, intrapartum intolerance, neonatal hypoglycemia, hypothermia, polycythemia; later metabolic/cardiovascular risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Tobacco/drug cessation, maternal disease control; low-dose aspirin when preeclampsia-risk criteria met

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incorrect dates: early ultrasound establishes gestational age
Constitutionally small fetus: reassuring interval growth and normal Doppler without placental disease

table.title: Patterns and delivery in otherwise stable disease
rows: Often later placental insufficiency; patterns overlap

human-papillomavirus-infection.name: Human papillomavirus infection
human-papillomavirus-infection.scope: Low-risk HPV and condyloma, high-risk oncogenic HPV (16, 18), anogenital intraepithelial neoplasia and carcinomas, HPV vaccination
human-papillomavirus-infection.core: Most HPV infections clear spontaneously; persistent oncogenic infection causes precancer, while low-risk types cause anogenital warts.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual skin-to-skin contact, new/multiple partners, immunosuppression, HIV
Smoking promotes persistent infection and cervical neoplasia; penetration not required for transmission

rows.label: Clues
items: Condyloma acuminata: painless flesh-colored, verrucous or cauliflower-like genital/perianal growths
High-risk infection usually asymptomatic; postcoital bleeding or abnormal cervical lesion needs diagnostic assessment
★ **Ulceration, induration, fixation, pigmentation, bleeding**, or nonresponse → biopsy rather than empiric retreatment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **HPV 6/11** mainly cause warts; **16/18** account for major oncogenic risk
High-risk E6/E7 interfere with p53/Rb → dysplasia and invasive carcinoma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical external warts → **visual diagnosis**; HPV testing does not guide wart management
Biopsy atypical lesions or uncertain diagnosis, especially with immunosuppression
Cervical HPV/cytology screens for neoplasia; abnormal results → risk-based colposcopy and directed biopsy
No routine HPV screening of asymptomatic partners or blood testing for infection
**Koilocytes** on Pap: perinuclear halo, irregular hyperchromatic nucleus → HPV effect/LSIL, not invasive carcinoma

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Warts: **imiquimod, podofilox, cryotherapy**, trichloroacetic acid by site/burden; older questions: podophyllum resin
Pregnancy: avoid podofilox/podophyllin; use clinician-applied cryotherapy or acid when treatment needed
High-grade intraepithelial lesions → site-specific ablation/excision; visible suspicious cancer → biopsy and staging
Treatment removes lesions without reliably eradicating virus; warts or asymptomatic infection: no antiviral

rows.label: Complications
items: Squamous carcinomas: cervical, anal (HIV), vulvar, vaginal, penile, oropharyngeal; recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
Warts frequently recur; treatment may cause local irritation, ulceration, pigment change

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **9-valent vaccine before exposure**; catch-up through 26 years, shared decision at 27–45 years
AAP: two doses starting <15 years; three if older/immunocompromised; federal 2026 policy differs
Vaccinated people still need cervical screening; condoms reduce but do not eliminate transmission

rows.label: Mimics
items: Condyloma lata: broad moist flat secondary-syphilis lesions, positive serology
Molluscum: smooth umbilicated papules; skin tags: soft pedunculated growths

hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.name: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.scope: Chronic and gestational HTN, preeclampsia, HELLP, eclampsia
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.core: Pregnancy-associated hypertension; maternal organ injury or placental dysfunction signals danger even without substantial proteinuria.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior preeclampsia, chronic HTN, CKD, diabetes, SLE/APS, multifetal gestation
Nulliparity, obesity, age ≥35, family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Headache, visual disturbance, RUQ/epigastric pain, dyspnea; edema nonspecific
★ Severe features: **platelets <100,000/µL**, creatinine >1.1 mg/dL or doubled, transaminases ≥2× normal
Other severe features: pulmonary edema, refractory neurologic symptoms
Presentation through **6 weeks postpartum**; eclampsia/HELLP possible without prior HTN

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormal spiral-artery remodeling → placental ischemia → systemic endothelial injury, vasospasm, capillary leak

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **BP ≥140/90**, either component, twice ≥4 h apart; severe ≥160/110 confirmed within minutes
CBC/platelets, creatinine, AST/ALT, urine protein; fetal growth US + antenatal testing
Proteinuria: **≥300 mg/24 h** or protein/creatinine ≥0.3; dipstick 2+ only if quantification unavailable
Chronic HTN + new proteinuria/end-organ injury → superimposed preeclampsia; HELLP: smear, LDH ≥600 IU/L

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Persistent severe BP ≥15 min → **IV labetalol/hydralazine** or immediate-release oral nifedipine within 30–60 min
★ Severe preeclampsia/eclampsia → **magnesium sulfate** through 24 h postpartum; airway before delivery
Chronic HTN ≥140/90 → oral labetalol/extended-release nifedipine; avoid ACE inhibitors/ARBs
Mg toxicity: areflexia/hypoventilation → stop infusion, **IV calcium gluconate**; oliguria → reduce dose

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, abruption, DIC, AKI, hepatic hematoma/rupture; fetal growth restriction, prematurity, death

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ High risk or multiple moderate risks → **aspirin 81 mg/day**, start 12–28 wk, ideally before 16
Postpartum BP review within 72 h if severe, otherwise 7–10 days; long-term cardiovascular follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: TTP: profound thrombocytopenia/hemolysis, persists after delivery
Acute fatty liver: hypoglycemia, jaundice, marked coagulopathy
Epilepsy: established seizure disorder; evaluate alternative causes despite obstetric context

table.title: Classification and delivery
rows: Before 20 wk or persists >12 wk postpartum
After 20 wk + proteinuria OR severe features
Severe BP alone sufficient; <34 stable → betamethasone
Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets
Deliver after stabilization, any gestational age

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate (own case), reason, communicate**; decision-specific, fluctuating
Competence: legal; diagnosis, age, alcohol use, incarceration, disagreement alone ≠ incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, even if life-saving or pregnant; avoid coercion, abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient
Refusing one therapy (blood) ≠ refusing all; provide other indicated care, including surgery

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no surrogate/directive/verified refusal → implied consent to treat
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or changed risk → renewed consent; consent revocable anytime before procedure

table.title: Who decides
rows: Ask whom to involve; facilitate promptly; no override
Minor decides; no parental consent (state law varies)
Parents seek unproven remedy for child
Continue proven therapy; investigate remedy; CPS not first
Close; discuss after waking; no next-of-kin consent
Autonomy ≠ entitlement; physician refuses, explains, offers alternatives

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

inherited-thrombophilias.name: Inherited thrombophilias
inherited-thrombophilias.scope: Factor V Leiden (activated protein C resistance), prothrombin G20210A mutation, protein C and protein S deficiency, antithrombin III deficiency, venous thromboembolism, pregnancy complications, anticoagulation management
inherited-thrombophilias.core: Inherited procoagulant states predispose chiefly to venous thrombosis; testing matters only when results change prevention or treatment decisions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: First-degree relative with high-risk thrombophilia, young/recurrent VTE, unusual venous site
Pregnancy, estrogen, surgery, immobilization amplify risk; homozygous/combined defects are higher risk

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT, pulmonary embolism; family clustering supports inherited predisposition but may be absent
★ **Heparin resistance** suggests antithrombin deficiency; neonatal purpura fulminans suggests severe protein C deficiency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Excess clotting activity or deficient natural anticoagulants shifts hemostasis toward thrombin generation
Older exams may expect **maternal uteroplacental artery thrombosis** → placental infarction/fetal loss, not cord clot

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm suspected VTE with **compression ultrasound** or pulmonary imaging before etiologic testing
Prior/pregnancy VTE + strong family history → **Factor V Leiden**/prothrombin DNA testing; PT/aPTT normal, cannot screen
Pregnancy/estrogen lowers protein S; warfarin lowers C/S; heparin and acute clotting alter antithrombin
DNA assays reliable during acute clots; defer functional assays until confounders resolve; don't stop needed anticoagulation
No routine panel for isolated miscarriage, preeclampsia, FGR, or asymptomatic general population; MTHFR testing unhelpful

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute pregnancy VTE → **therapeutic LMWH**; UFH when rapid reversibility needed
Nonpregnant VTE → DOAC or warfarin; duration depends on provocation, recurrence, bleeding risk
Pregnancy prophylaxis depends on prior VTE and specific/family risk; low-risk heterozygosity alone often needs surveillance
★ Prior unprovoked/estrogen-related VTE generally warrants antepartum prophylaxis; prior VTE → postpartum prophylaxis
Protein C/S deficiency: overlap heparin when starting warfarin; avoid unopposed loading

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent embolism, post-thrombotic syndrome; anticoagulants → bleeding, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
Inherited thrombophilia does not establish causation for pregnancy loss; empiric heparin does not improve unexplained loss

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Avoid **estrogen-containing contraception** in high-risk thrombophilia/VTE; prophylaxis during major transient risks

rows.label: Mimics
items: APS: acquired antibodies, arterial events and characteristic obstetric morbidity
Cancer-associated thrombosis: acquired hypercoagulability with systemic/malignancy findings

inherited-thrombophilias.evidence: Pregnancy prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [ASH teaching guidance](https://www.hematology.org/-/media/hematology/files/clinicians/guidelines/vte/ash-teaching-slide-setvtepregnancypdffinal71923.pdf); remaining content established hematology.

intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.name: Intrapartum fetal monitoring
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.scope: Baseline fetal heart rate, variability, early decelerations, late decelerations, variable decelerations, category I II III tracings, intrauterine resuscitation
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.core: Fetal oxygenation assessment from baseline, variability, and decelerations; persistent category III requires expedited delivery after immediate resuscitation.

rows.label: Definition
items: ★ Normal baseline **110–160/min**; moderate variability **6–25 beats/min**
Bradycardia <110; tachycardia >160; baseline change lasts ≥10 minutes
Tachysystole: >5 contractions/10 minutes over 30 minutes; oxytocin excess → late decelerations

rows.label: Interpret
items: Early: mirrors contraction → head compression; benign
Late: nadir after contraction peak → uteroplacental insufficiency
Variable: abrupt fall → cord compression; prolonged: 2–10 minutes

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Category II: lateral positioning, stop oxytocin, IV fluids; correct hypotension
Persistent tachysystole with concerning tracing → **terbutaline**; recurrent variables → amnioinfusion
★ Bradycardia: exam for cord prolapse; post-epidural → **maternal hypotension**; prepare delivery

rows.label: Compare
items: **Maternal fever** commonest tachycardia, variability kept; hypoxia → low variability, late decelerations
Transient minimal variability, no decelerations → **fetal sleep**, usually <40 minutes
Late decelerations → hypoxemia → **metabolic acidosis**; acute cord compression → respiratory acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Oxygen only for **maternal hypoxemia**; older routine-oxygen answers conflict with current guidance
Moderate variability or accelerations strongly argues against current metabolic acidemia
Category II alone does not mandate cesarean; reassess response and labor progress

table.title: Three-tier interpretation
rows: Reassuring rate/variability; no late or variable decelerations
Absent variability + recurrent late/variable decelerations or bradycardia
Resuscitate; unresolved → cesarean unless fully dilated
Evaluate severe anemia; expedite if persistent

menopause.name: Menopause
menopause.scope: Perimenopause, menopause transition, vasomotor symptoms, genitourinary syndrome of menopause, HRT
menopause.core: Menopause is 12 months without menses from ovarian follicle depletion; manage bothersome symptoms according to uterine status and hormone-treatment risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Natural transition typically in late 40s–50s; smoking, oophorectomy, chemotherapy or pelvic radiation accelerate onset
Menopause before 40 suggests primary ovarian insufficiency and requires a separate evaluation

rows.label: Clues
items: Perimenopause: variable cycles, skipped periods, fertility remains; isolated irregularity → **reassurance**, no biopsy
Vasomotor episodes: abrupt heat, flushing, sweating, disturbed sleep; mood symptoms can coexist
Genitourinary syndrome: dryness, dyspareunia, urinary urgency and recurrent UTIs; pale thin friable mucosa
Urogenital estrogen loss: **negative cultures**, possible sterile pyuria; friable mucosa → spotting, postcoital bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ↓Follicles → ↓estradiol/inhibin and ↑FSH; hypothalamic thermoregulatory changes drive hot flashes
Urogenital estrogen deficiency thins epithelium, raises vaginal pH and changes flora

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical symptoms at **≥45 years → clinical diagnosis**; routine FSH unnecessary
Unexpected amenorrhea → pregnancy test; earlier menopause → FSH/estradiol and targeted thyroid/prolactin evaluation
Postmenopausal bleeding → endometrial evaluation; do not attribute to normal transition
Hormonal contraception alters bleeding/FSH interpretation; amenorrhea on contraception alone does not establish menopause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Bothersome hot flashes, low risk, generally <60 or within 10 years → **systemic estrogen**
★ Intact uterus → **add progestogen**; hysterectomy → estrogen alone usually sufficient
Avoid systemic hormones with unexplained bleeding, estrogen-sensitive cancer, prior VTE/stroke/MI or active liver disease
Hormones unsuitable → **venlafaxine, paroxetine or gabapentin**; selected fezolinetant requires liver monitoring
★ Isolated GSM → lubricants/moisturizers then **low-dose vaginal estrogen**; routine progestogen generally unnecessary

rows.label: Complications
items: Bone loss, fracture, sexual dysfunction; oral systemic estrogen increases VTE/stroke risk
Combined systemic hormones can increase breast cancer risk; unopposed uterine estrogen causes endometrial hyperplasia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight-bearing exercise, adequate calcium/vitamin D, smoking cessation; age/risk-based osteoporosis screening
Hormone treatment not for primary cardiovascular/dementia prevention; reassess symptoms and risks periodically
Continue contraception during transition until menopause criteria met; menopausal hormones do not prevent pregnancy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: persistent heat intolerance, tachycardia, suppressed TSH
Pregnancy: positive hCG despite irregular cycles

microcytic-anemia.name: Microcytic anemia
microcytic-anemia.scope: Iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease, thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia
microcytic-anemia.core: Low hemoglobin with MCV <80 fL: distinguish depleted iron, inflammatory iron sequestration, globin underproduction, and defective heme synthesis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Menstrual/GI blood loss, pregnancy, low intake, malabsorption → iron depletion
Chronic infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy → inflammatory anemia
Inherited hemoglobin disorders; alcohol, lead, isoniazid, myelodysplasia → disordered heme production
Preterm birth → low stores, screen toddlers; infant microcytosis → **dietary history** for excess cow's milk

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, exertional dyspnea; severe anemia → tachycardia, angina, syncope
Pica, koilonychia, restless legs suggest iron deficiency
Markedly low MCV, preserved hemoglobin, high RBC count, **normal RDW** (Mentzer <13) suggest thalassemia trait

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation → ↑hepcidin → ferroportin suppression, impaired absorption and iron release; cytokines blunt **erythropoietin**
Sideroblasts: mitochondrial iron accumulation in erythroblasts from impaired protoporphyrin synthesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear → ferritin**, iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation; ferritin rises with inflammation
★ Ferritin **<45 ng/mL in anemia** supports iron deficiency; normal result cannot exclude during inflammation
★ Adult men/postmenopausal women with iron deficiency → **EGD + colonoscopy**; consider celiac testing
Hemoglobin electrophoresis for suspected beta-thalassemia; alpha trait may require genetic testing; exposure → blood lead
Microcytosis + afebrile pain crisis, at-risk ancestry → **smear** for sickled cells (sickle–β-thalassemia)

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Iron deficiency → **oral ferrous sulfate**; intolerance/malabsorption or rapid replacement need → IV iron
Treat bleeding source; continue iron about 3 months beyond hemoglobin normalization; reassess nonresponse
Inflammatory anemia → treat underlying disease; selected CKD → iron ± erythropoietin
Sideroblastic: remove trigger, pyridoxine if isoniazid-related; severe thalassemia → transfusion/chelation

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency: developmental effects in children, adverse pregnancy outcomes
Repeated transfusion → iron overload, cardiac/hepatic injury; oral iron → constipation, dark stool
Four-gene α-deletion → **Hb Barts** (γ4) → severe fetal anemia, hydrops fetalis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate dietary iron, pregnancy supplementation, lead-exposure reduction
★ **No empiric long-term iron for thalassemia trait** without documented deficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute blood loss: initially normocytic; hemoglobin may lag volume loss
Hemolysis: reticulocytosis, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin

microcytic-anemia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA iron deficiency evaluation 2020](https://gastro.org/clinical-guidance/gastrointestinal-evaluation-of-iron-deficiency-anemia/); remaining hematology established teaching.

normal-and-abnormal-labor.name: Normal and abnormal labor
normal-and-abnormal-labor.scope: Latent vs active first stage, second stage, active phase protraction and arrest (oxytocin, cesarean), false labor (Braxton Hicks), operative vaginal delivery, labor induction
normal-and-abnormal-labor.core: True labor produces progressive cervical change; dystocia management depends on stage, contraction adequacy, fetal status, and descent.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Nulliparity, obesity, fetal macrosomia, malposition, cephalopelvic disproportion, inadequate uterine contractions

rows.label: Clues
items: Assess membrane status, presentation, fetal heart tracing, serial dilation, station, and maternal vital signs
★ Tachysystole: **>5 contractions/10 minutes**, averaged over 30 minutes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dysfunctional powers, passenger, or passage → delayed dilation or descent

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Active arrest requires ruptured membranes: no change after **4 hours adequate** or 6 hours inadequate contractions
Adequate: ≥200 Montevideo units (summed mm Hg/10 minutes); IUPC when external assessment insufficient
Prolonged pushing: >3 hours nulliparous, >2 hours multiparous; individualize by descent and fetal status
Failed induction requires ≥12–18 hours oxytocin after ROM; slow latent phase alone does not mandate cesarean
Presenting part unpalpable → **ultrasound** for lie/presentation before amniotomy; floating part → cord prolapse risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Protraction (<1 cm/2 hours) with weak contractions → **oxytocin**, amniotomy; established active arrest → cesarean
Tachysystole → stop oxytocin, lateral positioning; persistent fetal compromise → terbutaline, expedited delivery
★ Operative birth: full dilation, ruptured membranes, engaged head, known position, skilled operator; failed → cesarean
Unfavorable cervix → balloon or prostaglandin ripening, then oxytocin; avoid misoprostol after prior cesarean
Labor pain → **epidural** most effective first-stage; pudendal block covers second stage only

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal infection, hemorrhage, exhaustion; neonatal hypoxia
Forceps/vacuum → lacerations, scalp injury; vacuum → subgaleal hemorrhage, avoid <34 weeks or face presentation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Induce for maternal/fetal indications or offer elective induction from 39 weeks; no elective earlier delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Braxton Hicks: irregular, self-resolving, no cervical change → reassurance; GBS prophylaxis only in true labor/rupture
Obstructed labor: strong contractions, no progress; CPD (macrosomia), achondroplastic pelvis, transverse lie → **cesarean**, not oxytocin
Shoulder dystocia: head delivered, shoulders impacted; failed head descent at full dilation → CPD

table.title: Stages
rows: 6–10 cm; older exams may use ≥5 cm

osteoporosis.name: Osteoporosis
osteoporosis.scope: DEXA scan T-score criteria, screening guidelines, glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis, vertebral compression fractures, bisphosphonates
osteoporosis.core: Fragility fracture or markedly reduced bone density identifies skeletal weakness, often silent until hip or vertebral fracture.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Postmenopause, older age, White/Asian ancestry, BMI <20, parental fragility hip fracture, smoking, alcohol >2 drinks/day
Glucocorticoids, early or surgical menopause, hypogonadism, malabsorption, hyperthyroidism, immobility, rheumatoid arthritis

rows.label: Clues
items: Height loss, kyphosis, acute back pain with **midline point tenderness** after trivial strain suggest vertebral compression
Neurologic deficits, fever, or nocturnal pain suggest alternative spinal pathology

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bone resorption exceeds formation; microarchitecture deteriorates despite normally mineralized remaining bone
Estrogen deficiency increases osteoclast activity; steroids suppress osteoblasts and reduce calcium balance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Hip/spine DXA**; use T-scores in postmenopausal women and men ≥50
★ Hip/vertebral low-trauma fracture establishes diagnosis regardless of DXA; acute vertebral pain → **spine x-ray** before DXA
CBC, calcium, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase, 25-OH vitamin D; targeted secondary-cause testing
Younger adults: Z-score ≤−2 suggests below-age bone density; T-score alone insufficient

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Alendronate or zoledronic acid** for qualifying fracture, osteoporosis-range DXA, or high FRAX risk; raloxifene/estrogen contraindicated after VTE
Osteopenia: treat if 10-year hip risk ≥3% or major osteoporotic risk ≥20%
Oral bisphosphonate: fasting water, remain upright; avoid esophageal disease, hypocalcemia, severe kidney dysfunction
Very high risk → teriparatide/romosozumab then antiresorptive; stopping denosumab requires follow-on antiresorptive
Vertebral pain: analgesia, mobilization, short bracing; procedures reserved for selected refractory cases

rows.label: Complications
items: ★ **Hip fracture** → immobility, thromboembolism, excess mortality
Bisphosphonates: rare jaw osteonecrosis/atypical femur fracture; denosumab: hypocalcemia, rebound vertebral fractures

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Screen **women ≥65**, younger postmenopausal women at increased risk; evidence insufficient for routine male screening
**Smoking cessation**, less heavy alcohol outrank supplements; weight-bearing/resistance exercise, fall prevention, dietary calcium/vitamin D
Prednisone-equivalent ≥2.5 mg/day for >3 months → fracture-risk assessment; prevent with **alendronate**, not estrogen/raloxifene

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomalacia: defective mineralization, low phosphate, elevated alkaline phosphatase
Myeloma: anemia, renal injury, lytic lesions; metastatic fracture: destructive focal lesion

osteoporosis.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2025](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/osteoporosis-screening%20); treatment: established fracture-risk framework.

ovarian-cysts.name: Ovarian cysts
ovarian-cysts.scope: Follicular cyst, corpus luteum cyst, theca lutein cyst (hyperstimulation), mature cystic teratoma (dermoid), unilocular vs multilocular, surveillance intervals, cystectomy indications, cyst rupture
ovarian-cysts.core: Most reproductive-age ovarian cysts are benign; morphology, symptoms, menopausal status, and persistence determine observation versus surgery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Ovulatory cycles, early pregnancy; ovulation induction → **hyperstimulated ovaries**; very high hCG → bilateral enlargement
Postmenopausal adnexal masses carry higher malignancy risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Incidental mass, pelvic pressure, unilateral discomfort; sudden pain after intercourse/exertion suggests rupture
★ Sudden severe pain with vomiting → **torsion**; syncope/hypotension → major intraperitoneal bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Functional lesions arise during ovulation; dermoids contain differentiated germ-cell tissues

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Pregnancy test first; **transvaginal ultrasound** characterizes wall, septations, solid elements, flow, free fluid
Simple unilocular: thin wall, anechoic, no solid vascular component; multiloculation warrants closer characterization
Papillary/solid vascular components, thick septa, ascites → malignancy evaluation; CA-125 nonspecific premenopausally
Normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion; urgent clinical concern overrides reassuring imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Stable functional/hemorrhagic cyst → analgesia, recheck after menses; unresolved → repeat ultrasound in **6–12 weeks**
Asymptomatic simple cyst above 5–7 cm premenopause, 3–5 cm postmenopause → ultrasound around 6–12 months
★ Hemodynamic instability → IV fluids/blood and urgent laparoscopy; torsion → detorsion with ovarian preservation
Persistent/enlarging, symptomatic, large, suspicious mass → surgery/referral
OCPs do not hasten functional-cyst resolution; older exam questions may expect OCP + 6-week recheck

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemoperitoneum, ovarian infarction, reduced ovarian reserve after surgery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Ovulation suppression may reduce new functional cyst formation; counsel urgent reassessment for acute pain

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG with pregnancy outside uterus
Tubo-ovarian abscess: fever, cervical motion tenderness, inflammatory complex mass

table.title: Cyst identities
rows: Luteal/early pregnancy; tender mass, crenulated vascular wall, hemorrhage
Bilateral multicystic ovaries; regress as hCG falls
Young; complex echogenic mass; fat, teeth, calcification

ovarian-cysts.evidence: Simple-cyst thresholds checked 2026-10-30: [SRU 2019 consensus](https://pubs.rsna.org/doi/10.1148/radiol.2019191354); acute management established teaching.

polycystic-ovary-syndrome.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome
polycystic-ovary-syndrome.scope: Rotterdam criteria (hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, polycystic ovaries), metabolic risks, weight loss, oral contraceptives, ovulation induction (letrozole, clomiphene)
polycystic-ovary-syndrome.core: Hyperandrogenism and chronic ovulatory dysfunction after exclusion of alternative causes suggest PCOS; management follows metabolic, menstrual and fertility priorities.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, insulin resistance and obesity; lean patients can also have PCOS
Pubertal transition can mimic disease, requiring stricter adolescent diagnostic criteria

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/infrequent menses, episodic heavy bleeding, infertility, hirsutism, acne or androgenic alopecia
Acanthosis nigricans suggests hyperinsulinemia; obesity is supportive, not required
Rapid virilization, deep voice or markedly elevated androgens → investigate tumor rather than assume PCOS

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insulin resistance and ovarian androgen excess impair follicular maturation and ovulation
Absent cyclic progesterone permits persistent estrogen-driven endometrial proliferation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Adults: **2 of 3 Rotterdam** features—hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, polycystic ovarian morphology
Exclude mimics: **hCG, TSH, prolactin, morning 17-hydroxyprogesterone**; latter screens nonclassic CAH
Total/free testosterone; **clinical hirsutism/acne** suffices despite normal levels; DHEAS if adrenal source suspected
★ Irregular cycles plus hyperandrogenism → **ultrasound not required**; LH:FSH ratio not diagnostic
BP, lipid profile and **oral glucose tolerance test** assess metabolic risk; adolescent diagnosis avoids ultrasound criteria

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Lifestyle/weight management first for all; modest weight loss can restore ovulation in overweight patients
★ No pregnancy desired → **combined OCP** for cycles/androgen symptoms; cyclic progestin or LNG-IUD protects endometrium
Persistent hirsutism → spironolactone with reliable contraception; allow months for hair response
Metabolic risk/insulin resistance → metformin; less effective than OCP for androgen symptoms
★ Anovulatory infertility → **letrozole first-line**; clomiphene alternative, older exams may expect it; check other factors

rows.label: Complications
items: Endometrial hyperplasia/cancer, infertility, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, OSA and depression
Pregnancy → increased gestational diabetes and hypertensive-disorder risk
Gonadotropin ovulation induction → high multiple-gestation risk, so letrozole/clomiphene first

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular progestin exposure for prolonged amenorrhea; persistent abnormal bleeding → endometrial assessment
Periodic glycemic/BP/lipid reassessment; preconception metabolic optimization and folate

rows.label: Mimics
items: Androgen-secreting tumor: rapid progression, severe virilization
Nonclassic CAH: elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone
Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea: low estrogen with exercise/energy deficit

postoperative-fever.name: Postoperative fever
postoperative-fever.scope: Timing (Wind, Water, Wound, Walking, Wonder drugs), atelectasis, surgical site infection, intra-abdominal abscess
postoperative-fever.core: Fever after surgery: postoperative interval narrows causes; hemodynamic instability or focal findings determine urgency, testing, and source control.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Emergency or contaminated surgery, bowel anastomosis, diabetes, immunosuppression
Prolonged ventilation, urinary catheters, central lines, immobility; new medications or transfusion

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Shock, rapidly spreading wound pain, crepitus** → invasive infection regardless of postoperative day
Purulent drainage, dysuria, productive cough, hypoxemia, or abdominal tenderness localize the source
Persistent ileus, leukocytosis, recurrent fever after initial improvement → intra-abdominal collection
Incisional erythema/induration + minimal uterine tenderness → wound infection, not endometritis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammatory cytokines arise from sterile injury or infection; later onset raises infection probability
**Atelectasis does not establish the cause of fever**; historical Wind attribution lacks supporting evidence
Older exam questions may expect **atelectasis**: fever <48 hours + decreased basal breath sounds, benign wound/uterus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Examine first**: incision, lungs, abdomen, lines, urine symptoms, legs; timing alone never diagnoses
Stable isolated fever within 48 hours → observation; avoid reflex cultures or antibiotics
Focal findings → chest radiograph, urinalysis/culture, or wound culture; sepsis → blood cultures and lactate
★ Suspected deep abdominal infection → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**

rows.label: Tx
items: Sepsis → IV crystalloids, broad antibiotics, urgent source control; do not delay for imaging
Superficial incisional abscess → open/drain; add antibiotics for cellulitis or systemic illness
★ Intra-abdominal abscess → **percutaneous drainage + piperacillin-tazobactam**; anastomotic leak/peritonitis → surgery
Pulmonary collapse → analgesia, mobilization, lung expansion; suspected drug fever → stop culprit

rows.label: Complications
items: Septic shock, dehiscence, organ failure; missed anastomotic leak → diffuse peritonitis
Unnecessary antimicrobials → C difficile, resistance; immobilization → VTE

rows.label: Prevention
items: Preincision antibiotic prophylaxis, aseptic technique, glucose control; promptly remove unnecessary catheters
Early ambulation, pulmonary hygiene, mechanical/pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis when bleeding risk permits

rows.label: Mimics
items: Malignant hyperthermia: perioperative rigidity, rapidly rising end-tidal CO2, hyperthermia
Transfusion reaction: fever temporally linked to blood administration; stop transfusion immediately

table.title: Timing: clues, not diagnostic rules
rows: Sterile inflammation; aspiration; dangerous early wound infection
Walking: VTE; Wonder drugs: drug fever, eosinophilia

postoperative-fever.evidence: Atelectasis evidence checked 2026-10-30: [Chest systematic review, 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21527508/); remaining management: established surgical teaching.

postpartum-care.name: Postpartum care
postpartum-care.scope: Normal puerperal changes, lochia, uterine involution, perineal and cesarean wound healing, breastfeeding, postpartum depression screening, routine postpartum visit
postpartum-care.core: Postpartum care is an ongoing assessment of recovery, mood, infant feeding, contraception, and chronic disease after every birth.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All postpartum patients; assess support, sleep, safety, sexual health, and reproductive goals

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Contact within **3 weeks**; comprehensive visit by **12 weeks**, with earlier risk-based review
Hypertensive disorder → BP within 7–10 days; severe hypertension → within 72 hours

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Edinburgh or PHQ-9 depression screen; assess suicidality directly after positive self-harm response
BP, bleeding, fundal tenderness; inspect perineum/incision for erythema, drainage, separation
Observe latch/milk transfer; frequent feeds, lactation support; cracked nipples → correct positioning

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Heavy bleeding (pad soaked <1 hour), fever, dyspnea, severe headache → urgent evaluation
Mood screen positive → diagnostic interview, psychotherapy/SSRI; psychosis → emergency hospitalization
Increasing wound pain/purulence → evaluate infection; breast fluctuance → ultrasound for abscess

rows.label: Traps
items: Ovulation may precede first period; discuss contraception before discharge
Lactational contraception: amenorrhea, exclusive frequent breastfeeding, infant <6 months
Postpartum hypertension and cardiomyopathy can first appear after discharge

table.title: Expected recovery
rows: Red rubra → pink serosa → white/yellow alba
Descends daily; near prepregnancy size by 6 weeks
Pain improves; pulling normal if intact; keep clean
Early cramping and fluid loss; breastfeeding intensifies cramping

postpartum-care.evidence: Visit timing checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG postpartum care](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/05/optimizing-postpartum-care); normal physiology established teaching.

postpartum-mood-disorders.name: Postpartum mood disorders
postpartum-mood-disorders.scope: Postpartum blues (onset <2 weeks, self-limited, reassurance), postpartum depression (MDD criteria, Edinburgh screening, SSRIs, psychotherapy), postpartum psychosis (delusions, infanticide risk, emergent hospitalization)
postpartum-mood-disorders.core: After birth, distinguish transient tearfulness from sustained depressive illness and from psychosis threatening maternal or infant safety.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior depression/postpartum depression, anxiety, poor support, trauma, sleep loss, pregnancy complications
★ **Bipolar disorder or previous postpartum psychosis** → especially high psychosis recurrence risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Anhedonia, guilt, impaired bonding/function, appetite/sleep changes beyond infant-care demands
★ **Suicidality, command hallucinations, infant-focused delusions**, confusion, mania → emergency
Unwanted distressing intrusive thoughts with preserved insight differ from fixed psychotic beliefs

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormonal withdrawal, circadian disruption, and psychosocial stress interact with mood-disorder vulnerability
Postpartum psychosis frequently represents a bipolar-spectrum episode rather than schizophrenia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale or PHQ-9** screens; positive result requires diagnostic interview
MDD: ≥5 symptoms including depressed mood/anhedonia, ≥2 weeks, clinically significant impairment
★ Screen for **bipolar disorder before antidepressants**; assess suicide/infant-harm intent, access, supervision
Check TSH/CBC for suggestive medical mimics; mania/psychosis → urgent psychiatric assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: Ensure safe infant care, assess support, address sleep; do not leave psychotic patient alone with infant
Depression: CBT/interpersonal psychotherapy; moderate/severe → SSRI, often sertraline during breastfeeding
Severe postpartum depression: specialist-directed zuranolone or other treatment; weigh sedation and feeding considerations
Psychosis: inpatient antipsychotic ± lithium; ECT for severe, catatonic, suicidal, or refractory illness

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, infanticide, impaired attachment/child development, recurrent depressive or bipolar episodes

rows.label: Prevention
items: Protect sleep, mobilize family support; prior severe illness → antenatal psychiatric plan and postpartum prophylaxis
Repeat mood screening through pregnancy/postpartum; establish follow-up before discharge

rows.label: Mimics
items: Postpartum thyroiditis: biochemical thyroid dysfunction with systemic features
Normal adjustment: transient stress without pervasive anhedonia or sustained impairment

table.title: Course and disposition
rows: Persistent symptoms; may occur throughout first year
Outpatient treatment if safe; escalate for severity
Emergency hospitalization; protect mother and infant
